title: Protecting Earth's Resources
seo_title: Grade 5 Protecting Earth's Resources Worksheets: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle and Clean Energy
standard_text: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on protecting Earth's resources (NGSS 5-ESS3-1): how communities protect land, water, air and living things, the three R's, renewable energy and data on water and energy saving. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Communities use science to protect land, water, air and living things.
key_sub: Reduce, reuse and recycle; clean wastewater; plant trees to stop erosion; protect habitats; and use clean energy.
body_html:
How to think about it

People use natural resources: land, water, air and living things. Our activities can harm them, but communities use science ideas to protect them.

ResourceWays communities protect it
Landrecycling, composting, planting trees, cover crops
Watertreating wastewater, saving water, plant strips along rivers
Airpublic transportation, clean energy, filters on smokestacks
Living thingsparks, wildlife crossings, replanting habitats

At home and school we can help with the three R's: reduce (use less), reuse (use again) and recycle (make into something new).

Example

Soil washes off a farm into a river. What could help?

Roots hold soil.

Plant cover crops or rows of trees.

Answer: Plant cover crops and trees.

Example

A 60-watt bulb is replaced by a 9-watt LED. How many watts are saved?

60 − 9

Answer: 51 watts

Common mistakes

  • Thinking reusing and recycling are the same.
  • Thinking renewable means it is fine to waste.
  • Thinking one person's choices never matter. Many small actions add up.
  • Choosing a solution that does not address the cause of the problem.

faq.q: How do communities protect Earth's resources?
faq.a: They recycle and compost, treat wastewater, plant trees to stop erosion, protect habitats in parks, and use public transportation and clean energy.

faq.q: What is the difference between reduce, reuse and recycle?
faq.a: Reduce means use less. Reuse means use something again. Recycle means break a material down to make new products.
Sources that nature replaces, such as sunlight, wind, flowing water and geothermal heat.

faq.q: Can kids help protect the environment?
faq.a: Yes. Saving water and electricity, reusing items and recycling all add up when many people do them.

items.q: What is a renewable energy source?
c: a source that nature replaces, like sunlight or wind
items.e: Renewable sources do not run out the way fossil fuels do.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
